Md. Atthar Alli vs State Of Odisha(Vigilance) .... ... on 18
October, 2023
Author: V. Narasingh

Bench: V. Narasingh
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Blapl No. 11390 of 2023
 Md. Atthar Alli .... Petitioner

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Mr. J.K. Panda, Advocate

-versus-
 State of Odisha(Vigilance) .... Opposite Party
 Mrs. J.R. Tripathy,
 Standing Counsel, Vigilance
 Coram: Justice V. Narasingh
 Order
Heard learned senior counsel for the petitioner and learned Counsel for the Vigilance Department.

2. The petitioner is an accused in connection with V.G.R. Case No.02 of 2023, pending in the Court of the learned Special Judge (Vigilance), Balangir, arising out of Vigilance Cell P.S. Case No.05 of 2023, Cuttack, for alleged commission of offences under Sections 7/12 of PC(Amendment) Act,
2018.

entities.text: Vigilance Cell P.S. Case No.05 of 2023, Cuttack
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 3. Being aggrieved by the rejection of his application for bail U/s.439 Cr.P.C. by the learned Special Judge,(Vig), Baripada, by order dated 30.09.2023 in the aforementioned case, the present BLAPL has been filed.

4. It is submitted by the learned counsel that the petitioner is in custody since 30.09.2023 and the allegation against him that he acted as a conduit to facilitate the co-accused Charls Nayak @ Naik,
who was the Tahasildar-cum-land acquisition Officer and demanded gratification for disbursal of land acquisition compensation.

5. Learned counsel for the petitioner also relies on the order dated 17.07.2023 passed by this Court in respect of the co-accused, namely, Charls Nayak @ Naik in BLAPL No.6677 of 2023 and seeks release, inter alia, on the ground of parity.

entities.text: Atthar Alli vs State Of Odisha(Vigilance)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 1 6. Learned counsel for the Vigilance Department, Ms. Tripathy opposes the prayer for bail in view of the conduct of the Petitioner and on instruction she submits that process under Section- 82 of the Cr.P.C. had to be issued to secure the presence of the Petitioner.
And merely because the co-accused has been released, this present bail application does not merit consideration.
7. Learned counsel for the Vigilance Department further submits that releasing the Petitioner at this stage would derail the ongoing investigation.
8. It is on record that amount involved has not been released but as rightly stated by the learned counsel for the Vigilance Department the same is by sheer providence.

9. Taking into account the release of co-accused, nature of allegation and as further investigation is likely to be based on documentary evidence, this Court directs the petitioner to be released on bail on such terms to be fixed by the Court in seisin over the matter.

10. Additionally, it is directed that the Petitioner shall not leave the jurisdiction of the learned Court in seisin without its permission till submission of final form and/or without intimation to the I.O.
and shall appear before the I.O. as and when summoned.
It shall be open to the Vigilance Department to seek variance of the order, if the Petitioner does not extend the desired cooperation.
11. Accordingly, the BLAPL stands disposed of.
12. Urgent certified copy of this order be granted as per rule.
(V. NARASINGH) Judge Soumya Signed by: SOUMYA RANJAN SAMAL
